newsitem.title: VIETNAM: U.S. envoy to Hanoi speaks of new era in relations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to Hanoi speaks of new era in relations.

text.p: The United States' first ambassador in post-war Vietnam arrived in Hanoi on Friday and proclaimed "a new era of constructive relations" between the former adversaries.

Douglas "Pete" Peterson, a Vietnam War veteran and former prisoner of war in Hanoi, said that while the issue of accounting for servicemen missing in action was Washington's priority, he hoped the two countries would conclude a trade treaty soon.
"Simply put, U.S. policy is to help Vietnam to become a prosperous country, at peace with its neighbours and integrated into this dynamic region," he said in a statement on arrival at Hanoi airport.
He added that he was confident the two countries, which normalised relations nearly two years ago, would in future not think of themselves as former foes but as good friends.
Sixty-one-year-old Peterson, whose posting was long delayed by domestic politics and legal wrangling, arrived almost exactly 22 years after the communist victory over U.S.-backed forces in 1975.
He takes over from Charge d'Affaires Desaix Anderson.

Progress on ties since normalisation in 1995, especially on a trade deal, has been painstakingly slow. Washington says it wants further progress on accounting for the 2,124 American personnel still listed as missing-in-action in Indochina from the war, 1,585 of them in Vietnam.
Diplomats on both sides concede that mutual suspicions still need to be overcome.

But signs that ties were strengthening came last month, when the two countries signed a copyright accord, a minor step towards the goal of achieving a full-trade agreement, which would lead to Most Favoured Nation trading status for Vietnam.
Officials say an air service accord allowing U.S. airlines to fly to Vietnam may be in place before the end of this year.

On September 10, 1966, on his 67th mission, Peterson's aircraft was shot down over North Vietnam's Red River delta. He bailed out and landed in a mango tree beside an irrigation ditch halfway between Hanoi and Haiphong port.
Peterson was locked up in the "Hanoi Hilton" -- which, in a sign of the times, has now been transformed into a swanky hotel and office complex -- until his repatriation in 1973.
The former congressman has made it clear that he returns with no grudges about a conflict that cost some 58,000 American lives and 6-1/2 years of his own youth in prison.
Vietnam's ambassador to the United States, career diplomat Le Van Bang, 50, was due to arrive in Washington on Friday.
